Article Title: Alternative-fuel passenger vehicles fast catching up with petrol ones
Article Text:
Passenger vehicle retail sales increased 19% year-on-year to 4.1 lakh units, crossing the four-lakh mark for the first time in July

NEW DELHI: Alternative-fuel passenger vehicles are on the verge of overtaking petrol-powered models in India, with CNG, hybrid and electric vehicles accounting for 40.6% of passenger vehicle retail sales in July, just behind petrol’s 41.7%, according to data released by the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA) Thursday. The gap has narrowed sharply from 13.2 percentage points a year ago to just over a percentage point, reflecting a rapid shift in buyer preferences.The trend came as India’s automobile retail market recorded its strongest-ever July performance, with overall registrations rising 25.8% year-on-year to a record 25.9 lakh units. For the first time, all six vehicle categories — two-wheelers, passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, three-wheelers, tractors and wheeled construction equipment — posted their highest-ever July retail volumes, underscoring broad-based demand across the industry.Passenger vehicle retail sales increased 19% year-on-year to 4.1 lakh units, crossing the four-lakh mark for the first time in July. Within the segment, CNG vehicles accounted for 24.6% of sales, hybrids for 8% and electric vehicles for 7.9%. While hybrid vehicles continue to use petrol as their primary fuel source, automakers classify them as alternative-fuel vehicles because they combine an internal combustion engine with an electric powertrain to improve efficiency and reduce emissions.Petrol’s share, meanwhile, declined to 41.6% from 47.6% a year earlier. FADA said fresh model launches, affordability gains following GST changes and consumers’ increasing focus on lower running costs supported demand for alternative powertrains. The dealers’ body also noted that uncertainty surrounding the transition to E20 fuel appears to have nudged some buyers towards CNG, hybrid and EVs.The transition was equally evident in the two-wheeler market. Electric two-wheelers accounted for a record 11.2% of retail sales in July, up from 7.7% a year earlier.Overall EV retail registrations across all vehicle segments climbed to an all-time high of 3.28 lakh units during the month, taking EV penetration to about 12.7% of total vehicle retail sales from 9.6% a year ago. Maruti Suzuki retained its lead in the PV market in July, retailing over 1.6 lakh units.
Article Summary: Alternative-fuel passenger vehicles are on the verge of overtaking petrol- powered models in India. CNG, hybrid and electric vehicles accounting for 40.6% of passenger vehicle retail sales in July, just behind petrol’s 41.7%. The gap has narrowed sharply from 13.2 percentage points a year ago to just over a percentage point.

Article Title: Survey: 81% of study-abroad aspirants plan to return home
Article Text:
Another 15% chose "applying for job" as their next step, without indicating whether the job would be in India or overseas

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The foreign degree may be global, but the career plan is largely homeward-bound: 81% of Indian study-abroad aspirants surveyed by Oxford International said they planned to return to India after completing their courses. Nearly nine in 10 were the first in their family to pursue education overseas, while almost half said the decision to go abroad was their own.The findings are part of the third edition of Student Global Mobility Index, which combines 17,925 responses to core questions with about 2,400 responses to additional questions on courses, family background, information sources and post-study plans. Another 15% chose "applying for job" as their next step, without indicating whether the job would be in India or overseas.The biggest shift over three survey cycles is in who drives the decision. Self-motivated students rose from 29% in 2023-24 to 34% in 2024-25 and 49% in 2025-26. Family influence fell from 59% to 37% and then 36%. Younger students were more likely to rely on family guidance, while older applicants tended to decide independently. Self-motivation was highest in north and south India; family influence was strongest in the west and central region.Academic choices were heavily concentrated. Seven in 10 were applying for postgraduate courses, and 75% identified business and management as their main field. Health and medicine was a distant second at 8%. Sciences accounted for 2% and engineering 1%.Google searches led 39% of students to their institution, followed by agents (35%). But Google's lead widened on trust: 56% named it their most trusted source for education information, compared with 20% for college events and 9% for Instagram. AI tools were trusted most by 6% and YouTube by 5%.
Article Summary: Nearly nine in 10 were the first in their family to pursue education overseas. Almost half said the decision to go abroad was their own. Self-motivated students rose from 29% in 2023-24 to 34% in 2024-25. Family influence was strongest in the west and central region.

Article Title: Temporary disability cert no bar for PwBD quota MBBS seat: NMC
Article Text:
Under the revised norms, candidates won't be denied admission merely because their UDID card or disability certificate is temporary.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Candidates cannot be denied admission to MBBS courses under the PwBD quota solely because they hold a temporary disability certificate or Unique Disability Identity (UDID) card, National Medical Commission (NMC) said. However, it made it clear that their disability status will continue to be verified by medical assessment boards (MABs) before they are declared eligible for counselling.In an addendum to "Guidelines on Assessment of Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) for Admission to the MBBS Course, 2026", NMC Wednesday said the change has been made to ensure that the guidelines are interpreted in line with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, 2024 Rules and a 2025 office memorandum issued by the department of empowerment of persons with disabilities.Under the revised norms, candidates whose disabilities are categorised as progressive, non-progressive or not likely to improve will not be denied admission merely because their UDID card or disability certificate is temporary. Their disability status, however, will continue to be verified by designated MABs before an eligibility certificate is issued. Candidates holding temporary UDID cards whose disability has been recorded as "likely to improve" will undergo reassessment before their eligibility is decided.MABs will also assess each candidate's functional competency."This year's revised guidelines unnecessarily created a new hurdle by introducing a distinction between temporary and permanent disabilities. I received multiple representations from students who were being harassed at assessment centres in Agartala, Mumbai and Delhi. That prompted us to submit a representation to NMC and raise this issue in the ongoing SC hearing as well," disability rights activist Prof Satendra Singh said.NMC said the addendum has been issued to ensure uniform implementation of admission guidelines and should be read as an integral part of the July 27 notification.
Article Summary: NMC: Candidates cannot be denied admission merely because they hold temporary disability certificate. Disability status will continue to be verified by medical assessment boards (MABs) before they are declared eligible for counselling. Candidates holding temporary UDID cards whose disability has been recorded as "likely to improve" will undergo reassessment before their eligibility is decided.

Article Title: Settling with a few cases won't stop CBI probe: Supreme Court warns realtors
Article Text:
SC said in court monitored investigations, sanctions for prosecution should be granted promptly

Many bank officials found to have colluded with realtors, Supreme Court told

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has put a spoke in efforts of defaulting realtors to escape CBI probe by settling with a few homebuyers. The court said these builders would continue to be investigated for cheating homebuyers and siphoning off their deposits till the last of the flat purchasers get their property or refund.Many homebuyers had become parties to petitions filed by groups of homebuyers pleading similar cause – enormous delay in project completion by builders who have already received money through banks under subvention and the banks insisting on repayment in disregard of the fact that the flats are yet to be delivered.Advocate Pranav Sachdeva told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the court may allow those homebuyers, with whom defaulting builders has settled, to withdraw from petition and continue proceedings for the remaining homebuyers left high and dry by builders.Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for CBI, informed that the agency had completed probe in 18 of 50 cases in which CBI registered FIRs on SC’s orders. A total of 17 chargesheets and a closure report have been filed before competent courts.She said the chargesheets name several bank officials who were found to have colluded with builders. The agency has invoked provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act against them and CBI has sought sanction to prosecute the officials from State Bank of India, Bank of India, Uco Bank, HDFC and ICICI.SC said in court monitored investigations, sanctions for prosecution should be granted promptly and directed these banks to give necessary permissions within two weeks for prosecution of the accused bank officials. “Failure to accord sanction within two weeks would require banks to submit explanations to the court,” it said and asked CBI to share documents on money trail to ED for initiation of inquiry under PMLA.On some complaints regarding alleged defaulting builders in other states, across states, the bench directed the CBI to conduct a thorough investigation into the allegations of misrepresentation and other irregularities by entities such as Ozone group in Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu; Vivansaa in Bengaluru; Rudra Buildwell Pvt Ltd in Greater Noida, and Omaxe group in Chandigarh. A separate status report in respect of investigations into these builders and related banking institutions shall be submitted to the court.The main allegation, as crystallized by amicus Rajiv Jain, against these builders is that they don’t have ownership title over the land and have partnered leaseholders to construct housing projects. However, they advertised as if they owned the land, entered into agreements with homebuyers and financial institutions without the lessee being a part thereof and remained unaccountable for delay and default.Given the expanding workload, Bhati informed SC that CBI had sought additional hands from states for expediting the investigations but none of the states have responded to the CBI director’s request. The bench directed the DGPs of UP, TN, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Punjab to send on deputation required number of personnel, as requested by CBI, within 10 days.
Article Summary: Supreme Court has put a spoke in efforts of defaulting realtors to escape CBI probe by settling with a few homebuyers. The court said these builders would continue to be investigated for cheating homebuyer and siphoning off their deposits till the last of the flat purchasers get their property or refund.

Article Title: In MP village, kids risk lives every day, hop over dam pillars to reach school
Article Text:
Children in Vidisha district risk daily commutes across a river

Poll Vote & Share your view Is the current education system in rural areas, like Kakraua, sufficient to support students? Yes, it meets their needs. No, it needs significant improvement. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





BHOPAL: Children from Kakraua village in MP's Vidisha district are forced to risk their lives every day by negotiating a precarious line of concrete pillars across a check dam on the Betwa river to reach their school - a route they take to avoid a much longer commute.A video of the children hopping perilously across the wide gaps in the check dam has gone viral on social media, raising fresh concerns about local infrastructure and student safety.Kakraua has a school only up to eighth grade.The nearest facility offering education up to 10th grade lies 13km away by road. By crossing the check dam, the distance shrinks to roughly 1.5km, prompting nine students - five of them girls in the ninth grade - to use the risky shortcut daily.The village is part of the constituency of former CM Shivraj Singh Chouhan, who is now the Union minister for agriculture.The dam-crossing involves walking across a series of exposed pillars that stand about three to four feet apart.Students hop about 10 pillars each trip. Villagers say the gap between pillars makes the route hazardous, especially during the monsoon when surfaces become slippery and the river's current increases."We have to work in the fields, so we can't drop our children off at school and back," said a parent."They find it easier to cross the dam nearby... We only have two options: we either stop sending our children to school or continue sending them this way even though it's dangerous."The consequences of skipping the unsafe route are already visible in the community.A student failed her final exams earlier this year after missing school because she could not cross the pillars due to her short height; she is repeating ninth grade this year.Parents fear that continued reliance on the shortcut could lead to further academic setbacks or, worse, an accident.District education officer N K Ahirwar acknowledged the problem. "I visited the spot and informed the collector about this," Ahirwar said."I have written to higher authorities to find a solution soon." However, he did not provide a timeline for the construction of a safe passage for river crossing.Local residents are now pressing authorities for an urgent solution to ensure uninterrupted schooling without endangering children's lives.
Article Summary: Children in Vidisha district risk daily commutes across a river to reach their school. A video of the children hopping perilously across the wide gaps in the check dam has gone viral on social media. The nearest facility offering education up to 10th grade lies 13km away by road.

He said he had studied the organisation and found its members "very well-meaning, fair and just and for the right cause, not aligned to any party as such".He welcomed CJP's decision to remain an apolitical pressure group instead of contesting polls. "Being apolitical, it gives voice to the voiceless," he said, adding that this had been his advice to its leadership.
Article Summary: Sonam Wangchuk said his wife Gitanjali had tried to get Rahul Gandhi to offer him juice to end his 26-day hunger strike at Jantar Mantar. Wangchuk also accused Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh of breaking a promise not to release photos of them offering him soup.

Article Title: UPI charges: Lok Sabha passes bill for government to make changes
Article Text:
The FM said the charge will apply to merchants and not to users and will help banks and fintech invest in infrastructure and innovation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha on Thursday passed a Bill that seeks to ease tax rules to attract investments and remove the existing legal provision that prevents banks and payment service providers from charging Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on notified electronic payment modes.The Bill — passed without discussion amid din — also proposes to remove the linkage between the Payment and Settlement Systems Act and the I-Tax Act and give legal backing to the government to modify the zero-MDR framework on UPI and RuPay card transactions. Outside the House, however, there was an exchange between FM Nirmala Sitharaman and Congress MP Jairam Ramesh. Ramesh said the Bill opens the doors for MDR. The FM responded, saying the charge will apply to merchants and not to users and will help banks and fintech invest in infrastructure and innovation.“More importantly, the UPI and services steering committee headed by NPCI is yet to decide on the MDR. This will happen after Parliament passes the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026... All this could have been discussed on the floor of the House if your party @INCIndia (Congress) engages constructively in Parliament when the Bill was/is tabled,” she said.While leaving person-to-payments outside MDR’s ambit, banks and fintechs may be permitted to charge 0.25% to 0.4% on payments to businesses in excess of Rs 2,000 with an overall ceiling on how much can be charged.Officials have argued that the levy will be lower than what is charged on credit and debit cards, and most merchants will not pass it on to consumers.
Article Summary: The Bill also proposes to remove the linkage between the Payment and Settlement Systems Act and the I-Tax Act. Outside the House, there was an exchange between FM Nirmala Sitharaman and Congress MP Jairam Ramesh. The FM said the charge will apply to merchants and not to users.

Article Title: Can't exclude SC/ST creamy layer from quotas: Government to Supreme Court
Article Text:
The Centre maintained that altering reservation policies requires empirical research and legislative action.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Opposing the application of the 'creamy layer' criterion for exclusion of affluent members of scheduled caste and scheduled tribe communities from benefits of reservation in jobs and admissions to educational institutions, the government has told the Supreme Court that discrimination against SCs/STs and OBC/SEBC communities do not happen only due to economic considerations."Keeping the broader concept of equality in view, discrimination against SC, ST and OBC/SEBC communities do not happen only based on economic conditions. The system of reservation aims to provide fair opportunities, reduce economic disparities, and foster diversity in governance and academia by addressing historical marginalisation," it said.On Aug 1, 2024, a seven-judge top court verdict permitted states to sub-categorise castes within SC communities based on socio-economic backwardness and the degree of under-representation in government jobs to ensure that the larger pie of 15% quota goes to the most backward. The court had asked governments to devise suitable criteria to bar the 'creamy layer' among the Supreme Court from availing reservation.Filing the affidavit nearly a year after Supreme Court sought response to a PIL by two people - one belonging to SC community and the other to OBC category - on Aug 11 last year, the government said, "Modification of reservation policy, particularly to introduce income-based preferences within reserved categories, should be preceded by a holistic review and thorough empirical study, including socio-economic data of reserved category beneficiaries" and could be done only by Parliament.Parliament alone can modify the list of SC and ST communities entitled to quota, it further stressed.Elaborating upon, it said caste, tribe or part of or group within any caste/tribe can be included or excluded from the list of SCs or STs issued under Articles 341(1) and 342 only by Parliament by law and it is not open to state governments or courts or tribunals or any other authority to modify, amend or alter the list of SCs or STs specified in the notification issued under Clause (1) of Article 341 or 342.Now similar provisions have been made for Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBC) through the Constitution (One Hundred and Second Amendment) Act, 2018, it said.The government said, "In the majority of schemes of welfare and development of SC, ST, and SEBC, excepting reservation in educational institutions and reservation in services under the state, there is a means test which ensures that benefits of schemes percolate to those who actually deserve them."
Article Summary: The Centre maintained that altering reservation policies requires empirical research and legislative action. A seven-judge top court verdict permitted states to sub-categorise castes within SC communities based on socio-economic backwardness and the degree of under-representation in government jobs.

NEW DELHI: Flooded with queries on Instagram about his stand on the ongoing Jharkhand students’ protests, Rahul Gandhi on Thursday said every government should try to change an education system that has “collapsed” and is “expensive and oppressive”, be it government of Congress or national government or of Jharkhand.He said students in the country are protesting against a flawed education system.The remark is significant as his party, Congress, is part of the JMM-led governing coalition in Jharkhand. The youngsters included Rhiya Ahir whose photo went viral for blocking a Mumbai police van, and Muskaan Sharma, who was the victim of a cop “jabbing a baton in her buttocks” at Jantar Mantar on July 20.As Rahul stood next to the protesters at the news conference, Farah Naaz alleged that in police detention, she faced communal barbs, with a cop even calling her “anti-national”. Muskaan said she was assumed to be a Muslim, which makes an Indian “fair game”, though she is a Hindu. Nutan Toppo said a pellet gun was fired at her.Rahul alleged the governing party is sending goons to the homes of students and forcing them to apologise, with those apologies being subsequently accepted by PM Modi. “ They defended the Constitution and protected the idea of India and its future... They are so young and standing before the media. But PM and home minister (Amit Shah) have no courage to stand before the press,” Rahul said.

Article Title: Rijiju raises point of order, Kharge hits back at minister
Article Text:
Kharge said they had been demanding Shah's statement on police "excess" against students for the past 15 days and that the PM should apologise to students

NEW DELHI: Rajya Sabha on Thursday cleared the Appropriation Bill, 2026, which authorises withdrawal of funds from the Consolidated Fund of India to cover excess expenditure of around Rs 54,067 crore incurred on certain services during the financial year that ended on March 31, 2023. The bill was returned to Lok Sabha after the members' approval through a voice vote - completing the parliamentary process for a Money Bill.During the day, RS saw multiple adjournments, as the opposition members demanded home minister Amit Shah 's presence in the House, leading to RS chairperson C P Radhakrishnan asking parliamentary affairs minister, Kiren Rijiju to convey their sentiments to Shah.In the morning session, the upper House saw two adjournments amid the opposition members also demanding that the chairperson allow the leader of the opposition, Mallikarjun Kharge , to speak. Amid repeated appeals of the chair to the opposition MPs to go back to their seats before he could call LoP, Rijiju raised a point of order. Citing rules, he said Kharge has been saying the same thing every day, and that is a rule against repetition.When the House reconvened at noon, protests continued. Heeding the opposition's request, the chairperson asked Kharge to speak. But the treasury benches objected to this. Amid protests from both sides, Kharge said, "If I don't read the rules, if I don't read my matter, should I read what you (Rijiju) give? It's my right, what to speak, when to speak, how to speak."Kharge said they have been asking PM and Shah to come to the House. "We request the chair to direct the home minister to come and give a statement...," he said. Rijiju objected that Kharge cannot dictate which minister should come on which date. Responding to this, Radhakrishnan said, "No, he (Kharge) is not dictating. He has put his request... As parliamentary affairs minister, you have to reflect the sentiments to HM..."In a press conference, Kharge said they had been demanding Shah's statement on police "excess" against students for the past 15 days and that the PM should apologise to students, but both have been absent from Parliament. "We requested the RS chair that we want the PM's apology and the HM's statement," he said.
Article Summary: The Appropriation Bill, 2026 authorises withdrawal of funds from the Consolidated Fund of India to cover excess expenditure of around Rs 54,067 crore incurred on certain services. The bill was returned to Lok Sabha after the members' approval through a voice vote - completing the parliamentary process for a Money Bill.

Article Title: Need to seal alliance deal with SP soon for UP polls, MPs tell Congress leadership
Article Text:
Sources said Rahul Gandhi called a meeting with UP Congress MPs on Tuesday, where he sought the views of Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha members

NEW DELHI: Congress MPs from Uttar Pradesh have told the party leadership that there should be an alliance with the Samajwadi Party for the 2027 assembly elections, brightening the prospects of a joint challenge to the governing BJP amid continuing pinpricks from local Congress functionaries.Sources said Rahul Gandhi called a meeting with UP Congress MPs on Tuesday, where he sought the views of Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha members on the upcoming assembly polls. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra sat with Rahul during the session.Sources said the MPs expressed a unanimous view that there should be an alliance with SP, and it should be clinched quickly. The urgency shown by the members ties in with the growing perception that the posturing by local functionaries and their angry exchanges are sending out a negative message of discord to supporters. SP and Congress together bested BJP in UP in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls.However, sources said, the MPs also underlined that the Congress leadership should secure “quality seats” from SP. The stress was as much on winnable seats as on numbers.According to sources, Rahul did not give any idea about the alliance or the tally that the party has in mind for negotiations with SP.The meeting was attended by Pramod Tiwari, Rajiv Shukla, Imran Pratapgarhi, Kishori Lal Sharma, Ujjwal Raman Singh, Rajesh Rathore, Tanuj Punia and Imran Masood.Sources said one MP cited the example of Bihar elections in 2015 and 2021 to illustrate how the party should focus on winnable seats. While Congress secured fewer seats in 2015 but scored a high tally, its score fell sharply despite contesting a high number five years later.Many participants felt the mood of the meeting suggested that an alliance with SP would be finalised soon, and seat-sharing talks would start in earnest. It is said that the newly-appointed UP Congress in-charge, Rajendra Pal Gautam, has undertaken an exercise on seats, while the party has also ordered a survey to assess its strength in individual constituencies.In the INDIA bloc meeting in June, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had asked Congress to show a “large heart” and trust the judgement of the regional parties in states.
Article Summary: Congress MPs from Uttar Pradesh have told the party leadership that there should be an alliance with the Samajwadi Party for the 2027 assembly elections. Article Title: Netanyahu calls PM Modi, discusses bilateral ties, West Asia situation

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday received a telephone call from his Israeli counterpart Benjamin Netanyahu, with the two reviewing progress on various facets of both countries' special strategic partnership and also exchanging views on the current situation in West Asia.PM Modi posted on X that India-Israel Special Strategic Partnership continues to go from strength to strength. "Netanyahu and PM Modi also exchanged views on the developments in West Asia," it added.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi received a telephone call from his Israeli counterpart Benjamin Netanyahu. The two reviewed progress on various facets of both countries' special strategic partnership and also exchanged views on the current situation in West Asia. The affirmation of friendship comes at a time when Israel has lost many of its traditional supporters.

Article Title: Supreme Court dismisses plea challenging Delhi HC relief to Hinduja brothers in Bofors case
Article Text:
The case stems from the Bofors scandal involving the Rs 1,437 crore howitzer gun deal signed between India and Swedish arms manufacturer Bofors in 1986

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday dismissed a plea challenging the Delhi high court’s 2005 decision that had quashed criminal proceedings against the Hinduja brothers in the Bofors payoff case, effectively bringing an end to the long-pending appeal filed by advocate Ajay K Agrawal.A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and Vinod K Chandran refused to adjourn the matter and declined to entertain further submissions during the hearing.The petitioner, appearing virtually, sought four weeks’ time to delete the names of respondents who had died. “I’m seeking four weeks’ time for deletion of the names, as respondent nos. 1 and 4 have expired,” the advocate told the court.Justice Pardiwala questioned the continued pendency of the matter and remarked, “What is all this about the Hinduja brothers and the CBI?”When informed that the Delhi high court had exonerated the accused and quashed the proceedings, Justice Pardiwala said, “All proceedings were quashed. What is this? How many years have passed?”The petitioner responded that “The deal occurred in 1986.”As another counsel attempted to make submissions, Justice Pardiwala made it clear that the court would not postpone the matter. “No question of adjournment. It is a 2018 matter,” he said.Counsel appearing in the case argued that a separate appeal filed by the Central Bureau of Investigation had earlier been dismissed by the Supreme Court on the ground that the agency was already a respondent in the present petition and could raise all its arguments here.The case stems from the Bofors scandal involving the Rs 1,437 crore howitzer gun deal signed between India and Swedish arms manufacturer Bofors in 1986. The CBI had alleged that the Hinduja brothers received millions in illegal payoffs linked to the contract.According to the investigation, Bofors paid nearly Rs 64 crore in kickbacks, with secret Swiss bank code names including Lotus and Tulip allegedly linked to the Hinduja family. The Delhi high court, however, quashed the criminal proceedings against the brothers in 2005, a decision that remained under challenge until the Supreme Court dismissed the appeal on Friday.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday dismissed a plea challenging the Delhi high court’s 2005 decision that had quashed criminal proceedings against the Hinduja brothers. NEW DELHI: It is not punitive to hand out compulsory retirement to someone, particularly in the armed forces, whose performance is slackening over the years, the Supreme Court said Thursday while rejecting the plea of a CISF officer challenging his removal from service on the ground of poor performance.A bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar said compulsory retirement should not be seen as punitive but as a measure needed to ensure a high standard of efficiency and discipline in the force. "The object underlying compulsory retirement is to weed out the dead wood so as to maintain a high standard of efficiency and integrity in public service," the bench said, adding such an order is "not punitive in nature", carries no stigma and is passed in public interest on the government's subjective satisfaction.It, however, said compulsory retirement is open to judicial scrutiny if the order is mala fide, arbitrary or perverse.Rejecting the officer's plea, the bench noted his performance had declined in the two years preceding the retirement order, with gradings dropping from "Good" to "Average". Members of disciplined forces are expected to maintain consistently high standards of efficiency, vigilance and discipline, it said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court: It is not punitive to hand out compulsory retirement to someone whose performance is slackening. It must also be judged by how safe, secure and resilient it is. NEW DELHI: Notwithstanding the progressive tightening of laws governing foreign contributions under Modi govt, their inflow has grown even though the total number of NGOs registered under Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2020, has declined.As per figures shared by home ministry last month, 2024-25 witnessed 16,200 NGOs receiving foreign contributions worth Rs 22,963 crore. FCRA registration of 22,496 NGOs has been cancelled so far, mostly after 2015 when nearly 10,000 NGOs lost their licences.In a recent statement, the ministry had addressed the criticism directed against the FCRA bill, particularly by Christian organisations. It underlined that "FCRA-registered associations are a small fraction of all NGOs operating in India. "The active FCRA database stands at 14,500 against several lakh registered NGOs," it said while asserting the proposed amendments target a specific, foreign-funded channel, "not civil society at large".The ministry also tried to allay fears that the proposed amendments would give govt unbridled powers to seize an NGO's assets, clarifying the designated authority shall manage only assets created from the foreign contributions and only once the organisation's FCRA registration has lawfully ceased."Vesting is initially provisional, with full restoration if registration is renewed, and places of worship retain their religious character by law in all cases," it clarified and added that the designated authority's orders would not be final but subject to appeal before the court of the district judge.As regards fears that the amendments specifically target a particular religion or community, the ministry clarified that it applies uniformly to all organisations regardless of religion, community or ideology.

SRINAGAR: In a bid to prevent illegal off-roading and disturbance to wildlife, Ladakh administration Thursday approved the introduction of India’s first-ever high-altitude wildlife safari on popular snow leopard and bird-watching trails in the Union Territory’s upper reaches.Ladakh is home to India’s largest snow leopard population — 477 of the country’s estimated 718 snow leopards. The UT also supports more than 38 mammal species, 340 bird species and 1,800 vascular plant species, which have drawn significant tourist attention over the years. Under this sustainable eco-friendly tourism initiative, visitors will get a rare, guided opportunity to witness the region’s distinctive flora and fauna, a government spokesperson said.The decision was made in the first governing body meeting of the newly constituted Snow Leopard and High-Altitude Nature (SHAN) Conservation Society, chaired by Ladakh Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena, the spokesperson said. Saxena directed the forest department to introduce guided jeep safaris on the lines of popular national parks like Kaziranga, Ranthambore, and others, using specially designed open-back vehicles driven by trained local drivers and guides.Apart from including areas like Nubra, Zanskar, Sham, Kargil and Drass — known to have sizeable populations of the elusive snow leopard and avian diversity — Saxena told the department to explore possible safari routes across Hemis National Park, Changthang and Karakoram wildlife sanctuaries, the spokesperson said. Govt will appoint 20 local youths and train them in bird-watching, bird identification, and spotting skills.They will be provided with all necessary equipment.SHAN Society, constituted by Saxena on June 16 this year, seeks to formulate a comprehensive roadmap for community-led wildlife conservation and waste management, and to promote plastic-free tourism, sustainable livelihood generation, and responsible eco-tourism across Ladakh through environmental education and empowerment of local communities.“These efforts aim at conserving Ladakh’s natural heritage so that future generations inherit an ecosystem that is richer, healthier and more resilient. Our vision is to establish Ladakh as a global example of community-led conservation and responsible high-altitude mountain tourism,” Saxena said.

NEW DELHI: Container Train Operators (CTOs) will now be able to operate across the entire Indian railways network with a single licence by paying a one-time fee, in a move akin to the National Permit system for trucks. The reform aims to boost containerised cargo movement by rail, reduce road congestion and cut air pollution, especially as nearly the entire railway network has been electrified and rail freight remains significantly cheaper than road transport.Introducing the major overhaul of the CTO licensing framework in nearly two decades, the railway ministry has approved a uniform all-India licence fee of Rs 25 crore, replacing the existing system under which operators paid Rs 10 crore or Rs 50 crore depending on the category of licence.Under the existing regime, concession agreements are valid for 20 years and may be extended by another 10 years. Under the revised framework, operators will instead be eligible for a fresh 20-year licence after successfully completing the initial 20-year concession period, with no additional renewal fee."The changes will be notified through a Gazette notification," the railway ministry said.As part of the reforms, the existing route-wise categorisation of licences will be abolished.The ministry said the simplified framework would lower compliance costs and provide greater operational flexibility. There are currently 22 CTOs in the country, and the ministry expects the new policy to attract more private operators.Existing operators will be allowed to continue under their current licence category until the end of their concession period. However, they may opt for an early migration to the new all-India licence by paying Rs 15 crore.The ministry said the uniform registration fee and the removal of renewal charges would reduce regulatory and compliance costs while simplifying the approval process."The amendments are aimed at establishing a simplified and uniform licensing framework for CTOs across the Indian Railways network. The reforms are expected to facilitate a streamlined approval mechanism while providing a common regulatory framework for container train operations under the Model Concession Agreement," it said.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday observed that the constitution of the previously undivided Shiv Sena had undergone a "significant transformation" over the years and eventually became "virtually a one-party structure. "A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana made the remark while hearing the Uddhav Thackeray faction's challenge to the Election Commission's decision recognising the Eknath Shinde-led faction as the "real Shiv Sena.""Originally, the party constitution was founded on democratic principles. Subsequently, it was amended and became virtually a one-person structure," PTI quoted CJI Kant as observing.Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for the Uddhav Thackeray faction, countered that the Election Commission had "no authority" to scrutinise the validity or democratic character of a political party's constitution while adjudicating a symbol dispute.In response, the CJI said that the debate goes beyond the Commission's jurisdiction and touched upon the larger constitutional expectation of democratic functioning within political parties."When we speak of democratic principles and institutions safeguarding democratic values, the question naturally arises whether a political party is itself expected to function democratically," he added.Sibal agreed that political parties should ideally function democratically but argued that they cannot be equated with constitutional authorities."But there is a distinction. Constitutional institutions perform constitutional functions, whereas political parties perform political functions. The standard of institutional integrity is necessarily much higher when a constitutional authority exercises its powers. A political decision can always be corrected. But a decision of the Election Commission, once taken in these circumstances, often cannot practically be undone," he argued.The hearing will continue on August 11.The Shiv Sena was founded in June 1966 by Bal Thackeray. After his death in November 2012, his son Uddhav Thackeray took over as party chief. The Shiv Sena split in June 2022, with one faction led by Uddhav Thackeray and the other by Eknath Shinde after the latter's rebellion.Following the split, Shinde approached the Election Commission, seeking recognition as the "real" Shiv Sena and claiming the party's name and its iconic bow and arrow symbol. In February 2023, the poll panel recognised his faction as the "real" Shiv Sena, a decision challenged by the Uddhav camp in the Supreme Court.In deciding the dispute, the Commission primarily relied on the numerical strength of the party's legislators rather than giving greater weight to its organisational wing.

NEW DELHI: The Centre for Policy Research and Governance (CPRG) on Thursday launched its Governance Dialogue series with a multi-stakeholder discussion on "District Led Development: Grassroots Stories, National Outcomes", bringing together senior bureaucrats, policymakers, industry representatives, academics and media professionals to deliberate on strengthening governance through district-level administration.Addressing the inaugural session at the India International Centre, Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS) vice chancellor prof. Badri Narayan stressed the need to bridge the gap between grassroots aspirations and policymaking."There is a real gap between how grassroots communities articulate their needs and how policy is conceptualised at the top, the language of the margins, the district and the policymaker are often very different, and what is needed is translation between them. That is precisely the gap platforms like CPRG can help bridge, by working from the bottom up," he said, adding: "Grassroots aspirations are changing rapidly, precisely because government schemes have succeeded in meeting basic necessities, and as development changes people's lives, it also changes what they aspire to next. The district is where this change must be understood, as it is not merely an administrative unit but a socio-cultural one, closest to the people at the margins."Delivering the keynote address, joint secretary in the Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development, Parikipandla Narahari (IAS), said: "There is often a gap between people's felt needs and their real needs, and closing it is at the heart of good governance. More often than not, the disconnect lies not in policy itself but in implementation, how a policy is carried out on the ground is what matters most for a policymaker. Once implementation is strengthened at the district level, the policies we design naturally come closer to the people they are meant to serve."Major General K. Narayanan, programme director (Security and Strategic Affairs) at NITI Aayog, who attended as the chief guest, said: "The soul of India lives in its villages, and the district is our basic unit of governance. It is here that policy becomes people, budgets become schools, roads and hospitals, and governance acquires a humane face. For a developed India, policies cannot be made in Delhi alone, they must be shaped from Leh to Lakshadweep. Real innovation happens at the grassroots, and development at that level rests on a few simple principles: trust the district administration, celebrate innovation, measure outcomes rather than expenditure, and learn from one another, for diversity is our strength. In the end, development is about people, and even the smallest village or a single woman entrepreneur can be a force to be reckoned with."The first panel discussion featured Jalna District Collector Ashima Mittal, Indian Oil Corporation Executive Director (CSR) Bibhuti Ranjan Pradhan and The Economic Times Senior Editor Anubhuti Vishnoi. Panellists highlighted community participation in district development, the use of artificial intelligence in policymaking, and the need to move beyond infrastructure indicators towards quality-of-life outcomes.The second panel, comprising NTPC Executive Director (HR) Premlata, National Centre for Disease Control Deputy Director Dr. Avinash Sunthlia, CNN-News18 Senior Associate Editor Madhuparna Das and CPRG Senior Resident Fellow Banuchandra, discussed integrating government schemes, strengthening grassroots healthcare systems and promoting citizen participation in governance.CPRG said the Governance Dialogue series will continue in the coming months to foster sustained engagement among government, industry, academia and the media on public policy and governance issues.

Article Title: Govt tightens rules on AI-generated content, cuts removal deadline to 3 hours from 36 & mandates labels
Article Text:

The government has tightened rules for social media platforms to tackle AI-generated deepfakes and other synthetically generated content, including fake audio, video and text.Under amendments to the IT Rules made in February, platforms must clearly label permissible AI-generated content and ensure it carries traceable metadata so users can identify “synthetically generated material”.The amended rules require platforms to take measures against unlawful AI-generated content, including deepfakes, child sexual abuse material, non-consensual intimate images and AI-based impersonation. Platforms must also inform users about the “legal consequences” of creating or sharing unlawful AI-generated content.The government has cut the deadline for platforms to remove unlawful content from 36 hours to 3 hours which shall start after receiving a valid notice from the government or a court. The rules also require intermediaries to deploy “reasonable and appropriate technical measures” to prevent users from creating or disseminating unlawful synthetic content.Significant social media intermediaries must use automated tools or other technical measures to proactively detect certain unlawful content, including material depicting rape or child sexual abuse. They must also make “reasonable efforts” to identify content that is identical to material previously removed.The government has also tightened grievance redressal timelines. Complaints involving sensitive issues such as nudity and impersonation must be addressed within 2 hours, compared with the earlier 24-hour timeline.Failure to comply with the IT Rules can result in platforms losing their safe-harbour protection under Section 79 of the IT Act, which protects intermediaries from liability for third-party content subject to certain conditions.The government said the measures are part of its efforts to ensure an “open, safe, trusted and accountable cyberspace” while promoting the “responsible development, deployment and adoption of AI” in India.

NEW DELHI: The Centre has selected 20 indigenous foundation-model proposals for support and sanctioned over 93 lakh hours of subsidised computing capacity as part of its effort to reduce India’s dependence on foreign artificial intelligence infrastructure and technologies.In a written reply in Lok Sabha on Wednesday, minister of state for electronics and information technology Jitin Prasada said the proposals were selected from 506 applications received under the IndiaAI Mission. They include 12 large multimodal models and eight small language models, with the intellectual property remaining with the developers.Among the models already launched are Sarvam AI’s 30-billion and 105-billion parameter models and Indus, Gnani.AI’s speech-to-speech model, BharatGen’s multilingual models and Avataar AI’s video-generation model.The IndiaAI Mission, approved in March 2024 with an outlay of Rs 10,371.92 crore over five years, is aimed at creating domestic capabilities in computing, foundation models, applications, research and responsible AI.The government has empanelled 15 computing service providers and approved subsidised computing support for 237 projects, involving 93.18 lakh GPU hours. It has also issued a purchase order for a high-performance AI computing system of around 1.1 exaflops at the National Informatics Centre’s data centre in Shastri Park, Delhi.Eleven national-level hackathons and innovation challenges have so far resulted in 62 AI prototypes, of which 20 have been deployed in public-sector institutions. The government has also approved 58 AI centres of excellence across states and Union territories. Of these, work has begun on 22 centres in 13 states and UTs.Another 13 projects have been selected to work on AI safety issues such as bias, privacy, algorithm audits, explainability and machine unlearning.Prasada said India was also strengthening the wider technology ecosystem through the National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems, which has an outlay of Rs 3,660 crore. Twenty-five technology innovation hubs have been established at academic institutions in areas including AI, robotics, cybersecurity, quantum technology and fintech.On semiconductors, the minister said 12 manufacturing projects involving committed investments of Rs 1.64 lakh crore had been approved under the Semicon India programme, with three having started commercial production.The Union Cabinet approved Semicon 2.0 on July 15 with an outlay of Rs 1.27 lakh crore. The programme will support Indian-designed chips, semiconductor fabrication and packaging units, and the production of materials, gases and equipment required by the industry.The government acknowledged that India’s AI computing ecosystem currently depends on imported graphics processing units procured through approved service providers. It said the IndiaAI and semiconductor missions were intended to progressively build domestic capabilities across the AI supply chain.Citing Stanford’s Global AI Vibrancy Report of November 2025, the reply said India ranked third globally in AI competitiveness and was the second-largest contributor to AI projects on GitHub.
Article Summary: The Centre has selected 20 indigenous foundation-model proposals for support. It has sanctioned over 93 lakh hours of subsidised computing capacity. This is part of its effort to reduce India’s dependence on foreign artificial intelligence infrastructure and technologies. The IndiaAI Mission is aimed at creating domestic capabilities in computing, foundation models, applications, research and responsible AI.

NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court on Thursday expressed concern over the impact of the Maharashtra resident doctors' strike on patients and warned the protesting doctors that it would order their salaries to be stopped if they failed to return to work immediately."We are concerned about the health of thousands of patients as well as the people of Maharashtra," a bench of Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad said.Questioning the doctors' decision to strike, the bench asked, "Why are you resorting to a strike at the cost of patients? Even if your agitation succeeds tomorrow, will you be able to bring back the lives of patients who may have died during the strike? Can the protesting doctors bring the dead back to life?"The bench, which took suo motu cognisance of the matter, also noted that the doctors had warned of suspending services in intensive care units if the deadlock with the Maharashtra government continued.Following the high court's observations, the Maharashtra Association of Resident Doctors (MARD) and the Indian Medical Association announced that the strike would be called off.The bench appointed senior counsel Vineet Naik and advocate Amogh Singh as amici curiae to assist the court and directed them to prepare a petition so that appropriate directions could be issued to prevent doctors from resorting to such strikes in the future.The matter has been posted for further hearing on September 8.MARD launched an indefinite strike on Wednesday to protest the Maharashtra government's decision to allow homoeopaths to register with the Maharashtra Medical Council (MMC) and prescribe allopathic medicines.Advocate general Milind Sathe told the court that, in an interim order passed last year, the high court had declined to stay the registration of eligible homoeopaths with the MMC and that the petition challenging the move remains pending.The court assured the doctors that the bench hearing the pending petition would take up the matter and decide it expeditiously.On June 30, the MMC issued a notification permitting homoeopaths who complete a six-month Certificate Course in Modern Pharmacology to prescribe modern medicines.

Article Title: Tarun Tejpal sentenced to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment in 2013 rape case; gets two weeks to surrender

PANAJI: Thirteen years after the arrest of a high profile editor-in-chief of Tehelka magazine, Tarun Tejpal , for rape in an elevator of a starred hotel, the Bombay high court on Thursday found him guilty of rape and sentenced him to ten years Rigorous imprisonment.The HC has granted him two weeks time to surrender.The sentence was pronounced in the State's challenge to Tejpal's acquittal by the trial court in 2021.After the court found him guilty, senior advocate Aabad Ponda representing Tejpal sought lenient sentence for him on the grounds that he is a senior citizen today, aged 62 and that the case is a 13 year old one.Tejpal addressing the division bench of Justices Dr Neela Gokhale and Amit Jamsandekar said he is a "political victim" and is 62 years old and a father of two with a wife and sought a lenient sentence.He said that there is so much evidence in favour of him that he can be acquitted ten times.Solicitor general of India representing Goa Government Tushar Mehta however argued for maximum sentence for Tejpal. He urged the court to consider that Tejpal was old enough to be in a parental position vis-a vis the survivor and argued that the sentence should set a precedent and have a strong deterrent effect.Mehta said that this was not some "misunderstanding or some banter" and pointed out that Tejpal had no remorse after the incident and alleged that he repeated the same thing on the next day.He said Tejpal was brazen despite resistance and despite the survivor saying no.He further argued that the survivor's mature conduct after the incident had been wrongly portrayed as that of someone who had enjoyed the molestation."It is high time the highest constitutional court of the state gives him the maximum sentence. No means No. You may be whosoever you are but when a girl says no it means no. That deterrent message may be considered," Mehta told the court while arguing on maximum sentence for him.Mehta during the hearings seeking Tejpal's conviction argued that the survivor was a stellar witness and stood by her case and that Tejpal's apology to her was proof of what he had done. He also argued that there was no reason for a man of her father's age to send her such her the 'the fingertips' text message after midnight and that it could not reasonably have an innocent meaning. Ponda had countered that saying the 'fingertips' text message had a different context and did not prove charge of rape.He had argued that the survivor had a "propensity to lie" and that her behaviour after the alleged incident was not commensurate with someone who had been raped and traumatised.
Article Summary: Bombay HC convicts Tarun Tejpal in 2013 rape case, sentences him to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment. The HC has granted him two weeks time to surrender. After the court found him guilty, senior advocate Aabad Ponda sought lenient sentence for him.

NEW DELHI: The death toll from the devastating floods in Assam rose to 95 after six more people died, while more than 1.6 lakh people remained affected across 14 districts, officials said on Thursday.According to the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA), six deaths were reported on Wednesday, two each in Sivasagar and Biswanath districts, and one each in Golaghat and Morigaon.Sivasagar continues to be the worst-affected district, accounting for 50 of the 95 deaths reported so far.Neighbouring Charaideo has recorded 21 fatalities, followed by Jorhat (9), Golaghat (5), Dhemaji (3), Karbi Anglong (2) and Biswanath (2). NEW DELHI: Air India's recent severe turbulence incident is now under a "thorough investigation" by the directorate general of civil aviation (DGCA), civil aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu said on Wednesday.Naidu said the Air India flight from Phuket to New Delhi experienced severe turbulence for "four to five minutes", leaving several passengers injured and some crew members with spinal and neck injuries.At least 17 people, including four cabin crew members, were injured after the aircraft suddenly lost around 300 feet in altitude during the midair turbulence.Addressing the media, Naidu said the aircraft was secured immediately after landing and all crucial evidence has been taken into the regulator's custody."In terms of why the incident has happened, we have immediately alerted the DGCA to thoroughly investigate the situation. BENGALURU: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) on Wednesday arrested another key absconding accused in the 2022 Praveen Nettaru murder case, taking the total number of arrests in the high-profile case to 25.An NIA release stated that the accused, identified as Ummar Farook M.R., was apprehended from Kochi, Kerala following a targeted operation based on credible intelligence inputs.Farook, an absconding accused had a Red Corner Notice (RCN) and a non-bailable warrant for arrest against him. The investigating agency had also announced a reward of ₹4 lakh for information leading to his arrest.The NIA had earlier chargesheeted Farook in connection with the conspiracy behind the murder under various provisions of the Indian Penal Code and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.Investigations revealed that he attended a conspiracy meeting at the office of the banned Popular Front of India (PFI) in Sullia town along with other accused.Investigation revealed that Farook had agreed to provide his motorcycle to a co-accused for identifying potential targets and conducting reconnaissance in Bellare village before the murder.He is also accused of participating along with other co-accused persons in an attempt to eliminate a protected witness in the case.The latest arrest comes weeks after the NIA, in July this year, apprehended two other absconding accused, Abdul Nasir P. alias Nasir, and Naushad, from Kochi in Kerala and Hosur in Tamil Nadu, respectively, in a coordinated operation based on information received from the Andhra Pradesh Police.The murder of Praveen Nettaru, a BJP functionary from Dakshina Kannada district, on July, 26, 2022 had triggered widespread outrage and led to the NIA taking over the investigation.NIA probe has revealed that the killing was part of a larger criminal conspiracy orchestrated by cadres of the banned PFI.In this case, two accused remain absconding. Efforts are continuing to trace and arrest the remaining absconding accused and to bring the investigation to its logical conclusion.

'Award will inspire those who serve the nation'

Doval accepts award with humility

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Saturday lauded National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval for his contribution to India's national security and foreign policy, saying the veteran intelligence officer has played a crucial role behind every major national security decision taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi since 2014.Speaking at a function in Pune after presenting the Lokmanya Tilak National Award 2026 to Doval, Shah said the NSA's advice and strategic inputs have been instrumental in strengthening India's security architecture and defence preparedness.He also said Doval's contribution to India's internal and external security had been so significant that history would reserve "a golden page" for him."NSA Ajit Doval has played a great role in strengthening India's foreign policy. In every decision of PM Modi for national security, Doval has had a 'role and advice' in the background," Shah said."Whenever history is written, if anyone analyses internal security and external security, then clearly, for Ajit Doval ji, a golden page will have to be kept reserved; there is no doubt about this," he added.Shah said one of the first decisions taken by PM Modi after assuming office in 2014 was appointing Doval as the National Security Advisor, a move he said transformed India's strategic posture."Today, India's foreign policy has become a foreign policy with a backbone of steel; no one can deny this. We have, along with self-respect, strengthened our position in the world," Shah said.Praising Doval's decades-long career in the Intelligence Bureau, Shah said India has emerged as a stronger and more confident nation under Modi's leadership, with Doval making a significant contribution to that transformation."After becoming NSA in 2014, Doval helped implement many strategic ideas on the ground and played a major role in modernising India's armed forces, strengthening technology, enhancing operational capability and improving the country's defence preparedness," Shah said.He added that the Modi government has fundamentally transformed both the defensive and offensive capabilities of the armed forces over the past 12 years, with Doval playing a key role in the process.Shah also noted that much of Doval's contribution can never be made public because of the confidential nature of intelligence operations.Recalling his tenure as Gujarat's home minister, Shah narrated how he first interacted with Doval following the Ahmedabad serial bomb blasts. He said then chief minister Narendra Modi had advised Gujarat Police to consult Doval while investigating the attacks."I remember Ajit ji had come to my house. The tips he gave resulted in Gujarat Police resolving not just the Ahmedabad bomb blast, but 13 bomb blasts across the country all at once. This was a very great achievement," Shah said.The Union home minister also paid tribute to Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, calling him one of the foremost architects of India's freedom movement.He said Tilak's iconic slogan, "Swarajya is my birthright, and I shall have it," gave a new direction to India's freedom struggle and inspired generations of freedom fighters.Shah added that the slogan made Indians realise that self-rule was their right and not a favour bestowed by anyone.Describing Tilak as a fearless journalist, Shah said one could truly understand courage in journalism only by reading the articles published in Kesari, the newspaper founded by the freedom fighter."How fearless a journalist can be can only be experienced by reading the articles of Kesari," he said.Referring to Tilak's role in mobilising people through the public Ganesh and Shivaji festivals, Shah said they laid the foundation for cultural nationalism and that India continues to follow the path envisioned by the freedom fighter."India is now moving firmly on the path of cultural nationalism laid down by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and no one can reverse that journey," he said.Shah further added that Tilak's ideas on nationalism, self-rule and social awakening continue to guide the country and remain relevant for nation-building, particularly for the younger generation.Shah said honours such as the Lokmanya Tilak National Award are not merely ceremonial but recognise those who dedicate their lives to the country and inspire future generations."When such individuals are honoured, the feeling of gratitude of society towards them is discharged... Today, the Tilak Award that has been conferred upon Ajit Doval ji... for those who live for this country and work for this country, it will become a place of great inspiration," he said.Accepting the Lokmanya Tilak National Award, Doval thanked the organisers and said he was honoured to receive an award named after Lokmanya Tilak."I am thankful for this award named after Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak and accept it with humility," Doval said.Doval also praised the country's leadership, saying, "We are very fortunate to have leaders like PM Modi and Amit Shah".
Article Summary: Amit Shah presented Lokmanya Tilak award to Ajit Doval and hailed his role in India's national security. He said Doval's contribution to India's internal and external security had been so significant that history would reserve "a golden page" for him.

Article Title: US makes $20,000 visa bond programme permanent; India not on 50-country list
Article Text:
India not on list

Who will be affected?

The US State Department has decided to make its visa bond programme permanent after successfully running it as a pilot scheme, expanding a policy aimed at reducing visa overstays. The programme currently applies to citizens of 50 countries.Under the new rule, consular officers may require certain applicants for US visitor visas to post a bond of up to $20,000 before a visa is issued. The regulation takes effect on August 3, when it is scheduled to be published in the Federal Register. US officials have indicated that additional countries could be added to the programme in the future, Reuters cites.The visa bond programme currently covers citizens of 50 countries, including Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan, but India is not among them. This means Indian applicants for B-1 (business) and B-2 (tourist) visas are not affected by the new rule at present.However, the State Department has indicated that more countries could be added to the programme in the future.The rule applies to applicants seeking B-1 (business) and B-2 (tourism) visas from countries covered under the programme.According to the Federal Register notice, "Consular officers may require covered nonimmigrant visa applicants to post a bond of up to $20,000 as a condition of visa issuance, as determined by the consular officers."The State Department said a year-long review of the pilot programme found that visa bonds were effective in encouraging travellers to comply with the terms of their stay in the United States.During the pilot programme launched in 2025, consular officers could require visa applicants to post bonds of $5,000, $10,000 or $15,000.Under the permanent rule, the $5,000 option has been removed and the maximum bond amount has been increased to $20,000.Immigration and rights advocates have criticised the policy, arguing that requiring applicants to deposit thousands of dollars could discourage legitimate travel to the United States.The visa bond programme is part of a broader immigration crackdown under President Donald Trump.
Article Summary: The US State Department has decided to make its visa bond programme permanent. The programme is aimed at reducing visa overstays. It currently covers citizens of 50 countries, including Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan. India is not among them. The regulation takes effect on August 3, when it is published in the Federal Register.

Article Title: 'Will march to PM's residence over E20': Kejriwal announces August 3 protest
Article Text:
Kejriwal accused the government of shifting its position on the issue

NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Saturday stepped up his attack on the Centre over the rollout of E20 fuel, demanding that consumers be allowed to choose between regular petrol and the ethanol-blended variant at fuel stations. He also announced a march to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence on August 3 to submit public petitions against the policy.Addressing a town hall-style meeting on E20 fuel at the Constitution Club of India in New Delhi, Kejriwal accused the government of shifting its position on the issue. “Government blaming opposition parties over E20 fuel, calling it our agenda, but now BJP leaders are also cursing them,” he said.Kejriwal alleged that ethanol blending would increase costs and create problems for both consumers and farmers. “Ethanol is costlier than petrol, farmers are in trouble as it is polluting water, soil; govt forcing E20 on citizens over India-US trade deal,” he said, claiming that India's ethanol imports would rise fivefold compared with last year after the introduction of E20 fuel.The former Delhi chief minister said he would begin collecting petitions at noon on Monday before leading a march with around 100 people to Lok Kalyan Marg. He also called for lower prices for E20-blended petrol and an overall reduction in petrol prices Kejriwal further urged the Centre to release the study it has cited to support the use of E20 fuel. "The Centre says studies have been conducted and E20 does not harm vehicles. I want them to share that report," he said.The event was attended by people from several states, with participants sharing their experiences and concerns about using E20 fuel and the issues they claimed to have faced with their vehicles.
Article Summary: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal stepped up his attack on the Centre over the rollout of E20 fuel. He announced a march to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence on August 3 to submit public petitions against the policy. Kejriwal accused the government of shifting its position on the issue.
